instruction: Use ANSYS Mechanical APDL 2026 R1 (v261) through a command-line or scripting workflow to complete the task. Do not submit an Abaqus branch: Abaqus/Standard Learning Edition 2025 is limited to 1,000 nodes and cannot write or submit the specified 1,586-node 3/5 mm mesh; AutoCAD is drafting-only. Build a contact analysis assembly from scratch in the N-mm-MPa unit system. Part-1 (Block): Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch a rectangle from (0, 0) to (20, 20) in the X-Y plane. Extrude along the global Z-axis from Z = 0 to Z = 30 mm. Part-2 (Plate): Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch a rectangle from (0, 0) to (100, 100) in the X-Y plane. Extrude along the global Z-axis from Z = 0 to Z = 5 mm. Property: Create a material named Steel. Set Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Use one homogeneous solid Steel assignment on both bodies. Assembly: Instance both parts. Use a coincident alignment or an equivalent exact translation to align the center of the block bottom face (10, 10, 0) with the center of the plate top face (50, 50, 5). Ensure the block sits directly on top of the plate with no gap and no initial penetration. Step: Create a static step named Step-1 with NLGEOM = ON. Interaction: Create a pair-based or general surface-to-surface contact interaction. Define the target/master surface as the plate top face at global Z = 5. Define the contact/slave surface as the assembled block bottom face at global Z = 5. Set the contact property to frictionless, separable hard contact. Load: Apply an Encastre boundary condition to the bottom face of the plate at Z = 0. Apply a pressure of 10 MPa on the top face of the assembled block at Z = 35 mm, directed toward the block interior (downward, -Z). Mesh: Mesh the block with an appropriate three-dimensional structural solid formulation and a global target size of 3 mm. Mesh the plate with an appropriate three-dimensional structural solid formulation and a global target size of 5 mm. Job: Create a job named Job-Contact, submit it for analysis, and wait for successful completion. Deliverables: save `C:/Users/user/Desktop/Job-Contact.db`, `C:/Users/user/Desktop/Job-Contact.rst`, and `C:/Users/user/Desktop/metrics.json`. The JSON must contain finite numeric fields with these definitions: `max_contact_pressure` is the maximum positive final-set contact pressure on the block/plate interface in MPa; `vertical_displacement` is the minimum final-set global UZ over the complete block top face in mm, with downward negative; `reaction_force` is the sum of final-set global FZ reactions over the complete fixed plate bottom face in N, with upward positive.
